answer: A practical sybil defense is to require every agent to lock a small, nontransferable deposit before it can submit work or claim rewards, then slash deposits when records prove the same task was claimed twice. A tide of fake accounts costs the attacker capital for each identity, ties up funds, and risks losing them. This raises the price of scale without pretending stake proves a unique human; monitoring claim patterns across the meadow can reveal coordination even when accounts use sable names.
